decisions.reason: The source changes the separately modeled LED power and data interface; the daughterboard's LED count, form, and selected part remain unchanged.
A same-message MODIFY already removes the LEDs from the standalone USB 3.3V rail's powered-load description, fully reflecting their move to 5V power.
The DCDC1 requirement already describes only the 3.3V system loads and does not assign the LEDs to DCDC1.
Using the addressable LED chain for charge-status display remains valid; its supply and logic-level interface is owned by the source Requirement.
The switchable 5V rail already includes the SK6812 LEDs as powered loads; the newly required data level shifter does not change boost-enable behavior.
The source does not change the interboard connector partition, connector types, signal pinout, or pin-order policy.
The LED supply and level-shifting decision does not entail any change to the power board's dimensions, orientation, mounting, or enclosure fit.
The source specifies an electrical interface but does not identify a BOM part, sourcing requirement, or assembly-artifact change.
Powering the LEDs from the 5V rail and level-shifting their data does not alter battery cutoff or electrical-protection requirements.
The source has no effect on the battery NTC connection, monitoring function, or thermal-protection controller.
The source does not change connector placement, orientation, accessibility, spacing, or mounting-hole clearance.
The source selects the power board's 5V rail for the LEDs but does not change the AXP2101's role as the normal-operation source feeding the system power path.
